title: Turnover and the Ellington ideal
summary: Why sidemen left and the wish for an Ellington-like band.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: When you had a road band, did you have a band turnover or did guys stay with you for quite a while?
They stayed as long as they wanted to. One time everybody left at once, and then we began having troubles--not real troubles, because somehow it
always shaped up again, but it began lacking the security that it had. Really, what both Bill and I wanted was an Ellington-type thing.
Where you're writing for specific people?

It was unfortunate that our names were there, because it gave the impression that we were entrepreneurs who were using people for our personal gain, which was not so. We both wanted to make it some sort of cooperative thing without ever really knowing how to do it and it would be unfair to do that when things weren't going too well. When things are bad, you make it cooperative and as soon as it gets good, you forget about it.
We don't know; it's all academic now anyhow, how that would have turned out.
Most of them got off the road because of family problems; they had to.
That was true of Moussey and Nick and I kept replacing them. Harvey Estrom had to go too.
